recipes.name: Oats Upma with Mixed Vegetables and Peanuts
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe provides complex carbohydrates for sustained energy, dietary fiber to support gut health and blood sugar regulation, and protein from oats and peanuts, beneficial for managing glucose and lipid profiles.
instructions: Dry roast oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds; once they splutter, add curry leaves, green chili, and grated ginger. Sauté for a minute.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add mixed vegetables and turmeric powder, cook for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil. Reduce heat, add roasted oats and peanuts, mix well. Cover and cook for 3-4 minutes until water is absorbed.
Turn off heat, stir in lemon juice. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Palak Paneer with Whole Wheat Roti
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is rich in iron from spinach, calcium and protein from paneer, and fiber from both ingredients and whole wheat roti, supporting hemoglobin levels, bone health, and satiety while being heart-healthy.
instructions: Blanch spinach in hot water for 2-3 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water. Drain, squeeze out excess water, and blend into a smooth paste with ginger, garlic, and green chilies.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, let them splutter. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and pulpy.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook for a minute. Add the spinach paste and cook for 5-7 minutes on medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Add paneer cubes and garam masala. Mix gently and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Set aside.

For roti: Knead whole wheat atta with water and a pinch of salt to form a soft dough. Divide into equal portions, roll into thin circles, and cook on a hot tawa until puffed and golden spots appear. Serve hot with Palak Paneer.

recipes.name: Masoor Dal Tadka
recipes.health_benefit: This lentil dish is an excellent source of plant-based protein, iron, and dietary fiber, which can help manage blood sugar levels, support cardiovascular health by impacting cholesterol, and contribute to iron intake for hemoglobin synthesis.
instructions: Wash and soak masoor dal for 15-20 minutes. Drain.
Cook dal with 2.5 cups of water and a pinch of turmeric in a pressure cooker for 2-3 whistles, or in a pot until soft and mushy.
For tadka: Heat oil/ghee in a separate small pan. Add cumin seeds, let them splutter. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and green chili. Sauté until fragrant.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, and red chili powder (if using). Cook until tomatoes are soft.
Pour the cooked dal into the tadka. Add remaining water if needed to adjust consistency. Bring to a simmer, add salt, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.

recipes.name: Grilled Mackerel with Lemon & Herbs and Brown Rice
recipes.health_benefit: Mackerel is an excellent source of Omega-3 fatty acids and Vitamin D, vital for cardiovascular health (HDL, triglycerides) and bone health. Lean protein and complex carbohydrates from brown rice further support energy and satiety.
instructions: Rinse mackerel fillets and pat dry. In a bowl, mix olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, chopped coriander, salt, and pepper. Marinate the fish for 15-20 minutes.
Cook brown rice according to package instructions.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Grill the mackerel fillets for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked through and flaky.
Serve grilled mackerel with cooked brown rice and a side of steamed or lightly sautéed mixed vegetables. Garnish with lemon slices.

recipes.name: Lean Chicken Curry with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: This curry provides lean protein, which is essential for muscle maintenance and satiety. Chicken is also a good source of Vitamin B12 and iron, supporting energy metabolism and hemoglobin levels. Mixed vegetables add fiber and micronutrients.

ingredients.item: Curry powder (or blend of cumin, coriander, turmeric)

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and bay leaf. Sauté for a few seconds.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes and cook until lightly browned on all sides.
Stir in curry powder (or individual spices), salt, and tomato puree. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oil separates from the masala.
Add mixed vegetables and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Chaat
recipes.health_benefit: This snack is packed with protein and fiber from sprouted moong dal, aiding in satiety and promoting healthy blood sugar levels. The fresh vegetables add vitamins and minerals, while the sprouts enhance nutrient bioavailability.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine sprouted moong dal, chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, green chili, and fresh coriander leaves.
Add chaat masala, black salt, and lemon juice. Mix everything gently until well combined.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack.

recipes.name: Cucumber and Carrot Raita
recipes.health_benefit: Yogurt provides calcium for bone health and probiotics for gut health, which can indirectly support overall metabolic functions. Cucumber and carrot add fiber and hydration, making it a cooling and nutrient-rich accompaniment to meals.
instructions: Whisk the yogurt until smooth. If too thick, add a few tablespoons of water to reach desired consistency.
Gently fold in the grated cucumber and carrot.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and chopped coriander leaves. Mix well.
Chill for at least 15 minutes before serving for best taste. Serve as a side with main meals.
